title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this part of 'Analysis situs' Grothendieck is axiomatizing combinatorial 'cell decompositions' of a set X. The data are a family 𝔛 = (X_i), i ∈ I, of subsets of X, indexed by an ordered set I. Each X_i is thought of as a 'closed cell' and has an 'open cell' X_i^0 = X_i \ ⋃_{j<i} X_j. The axioms he uses (labelled 1', 2', 3', b', b'', and α, β, γ) are:
- (a) each open cell is non-empty: X_i^0 ≠ ∅;
- (b'') the open cells are pairwise disjoint;
- (β) saturation, a 'frontier condition': each X_i is the union of the open cells X_j^0 contained in it.

Top of page: end of the proof that, under these axioms, X_i ⊂ X_j implies i ≤ j, so the order on I is recovered from inclusion.
- Take x ∈ X_i^0, which is non-empty by b'.
- By the covering result of the previous page (open cells relative to j equal the X_{j'}^0), there is j' ≤ j with x ∈ X_{j'}^0.
- So X_i^0 ∩ X_{j'}^0 ≠ ∅, and disjointness (b'') gives i = j'. Hence i ≤ j, qed.

Example: the axioms are not redundant; saturation does not follow from the others. Here 1' and 2' hold and all X_i^0 ≠ ∅, but 3' fails (3' is an indexation respecting inclusion, i ≤ j ⇒ X_i ⊂ X_j).
- Let A_0 ⊋ A_1 ⊋ … be a strictly decreasing sequence of subsets of X with N = ⋂ A_n ≠ ∅.
- Let A_∞ ⊂ X with A_∞ ∩ A_0 = N and A_∞ ⊄ A_0, i.e. N ≠ A_∞.
- Take the family indexed by I = ℕ ∪ {∞}, ordered by inclusion, with ∞ an isolated point.
- Then A_n^0 = A_n \ A_{n+1} ≠ ∅ and A_∞^0 = A_∞ ≠ ∅.
- These open cells are pairwise disjoint, since N ⊂ A_{n+1}. Their union is A_0 ∪ A_∞.
- But A_n is not the union of the open cells it contains: that union is A_n \ N, so N is missing. So A_n is not saturated for the equivalence relation defined by the partition into open cells.
- A point x ∈ N lies in no smallest member of the family Φ'.
- Also A_∞^0 ∩ A_i ≠ ∅ (it equals N) without A_∞^0 ⊂ A_i.
- So (iiβ), saturation, fails while α and γ hold.

Question at the bottom: is the right axiom system 'X_i^0 ≠ ∅ for all i, X_i^0 ∩ X_j^0 = ∅ for i ≠ j, plus saturation X_i = ⋃_{X_j^0 ⊂ X_i} X_j^0'?

In modern terms these axioms say that x ↦ (the unique i with x ∈ X_i^0) is a surjection X → I whose fibres are the open cells. The X_i are then exactly the preimages of the down-sets ↓i. Equivalently, it is a stratification of X over the poset I, i.e. a map to I with its Alexandrov topology, and the face poset is recovered from inclusions. The next page continues with a counterexample to 'X_j^0 ⊂ X_i ⇒ j ≤ i', obtained by adding the set A_∞ \ N.
errors: No mathematical error found. The example works: the A_n^0 are disjoint from A_∞ because A_∞ ∩ (A_n \ A_{n+1}) ⊂ N ∩ (A_n \ A_{n+1}) = ∅.

Minor slip in the notes: the opening line of the example says 'on a pas tous les X_i^0 ≠ ∅'. In fact all X_i^0 are non-empty in the example; what fails is saturation (3'/β). This is most likely a transcription issue.

ideas.what: Recovering the indexing order from inclusions of closed cells, using non-emptiness and disjointness of open cells
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of a cell decomposition / stratification; order recovered from closure relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (regular CW complexes, Björner's face posets; stratified spaces)

ideas.what: Saturation (frontier condition): each closed cell is a union of open cells
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition / poset-stratified set (map to a poset with Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney–Thom stratification theory; poset-stratified spaces (Lurie HA A.5, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)

ideas.what: Counterexample (decreasing sequence plus extra set meeting it in the intersection) showing that saturation is independent of non-emptiness and disjointness
ideas.modern_name: Independence of axioms for a cell partition

deep.surprise_reason: This is elementary set-theoretic bookkeeping for axiomatizing cell/stratified decompositions. The equivalence with maps to a poset is standard today. It is of only biographical interest as part of the 1986 'Analysis situs' project.
transcription_corrections: The page number at the top is '44', not '99' (the previous page is 43, the next is 45).
'On prend I ∈ 𝔓(X)' should read 'On prend I ⊂ 𝔓(X)', the family defined by the A_i (i ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}), ordered by inclusion, ∞ being an isolated point.
'un x ∈ N n'est pas contenu dans un plus petit élément de Φ'' should read 'Un x ∈ N n'est pas contenu dans un plus petit élément de Φ''; the inserted '= N' is a marginal note.
'A_∞ ∩ A_i (≠∅)' should be read with A_∞^0 ∩ A_i (= N) written below; the meaning is that A_∞^0 ∩ A_i ≠ ∅ without A_∞^0 ⊂ A_i.
The first line of the example likely reads '…où on a 1' et 2', et on a bien tous les X_i^0 ≠ ∅, sans avoir 3' (indexation respectant la relation d'inclusion i ≤ j ⇒ X_i ⊂ X_j)'.
First line of the page: 'par ce qui précède, ∃ j' ≤ j avec x ∈ X_{j'}^{0'}, or [on a vu que] X_{j'}^{0'} = X_{j'}^0'.
